title: थरी थरीका पटचित्र [Various types of paintings]
authors: रञ्जितकार Ranjitkar, जुनु बासुकला Junu Basukala
nepali: कपडामा लेखिएको चित्रलाई संस्कृत र नेपाली भाषामा ‘पटचित्र’, नेपालभाषामा ‘पौभाः’ र तिब्बती भाषामा ‘थान्का’ भनिन्छ । कपडाका आकार प्रकार र चित्र लेख्ने विशेषताका आधारमा पटचित्रलाई सात प्रकारमा विभाजन गर्न सकिन्छ — पौभाः चित्र, पटमण्डल, बिलंपौ, धकिंचित्र, हलिपटचित्र, गाछिका चित्र र इलां चित्र । पौभाः चित्र भन्नाले चारपाटे कपडामाथि देवी देवता, धार्मिक अनुष्ठान, समाजमा घटित ऐतिहासिक घटना विशेषको संस्मरण, सामाजिक अवस्था र प्राकृतिक तथा मानवद्वारा निर्मित दृश्य आदि सम्बन्धी चित्रणलाई भनिन्छ । पटमण्डलमा कपडामा मुख्य देवतालाई केन्द्रमा राखेर ज्यामितीय आकारहरूमा ससाना देवताहरूको चित्रबनाउने वा ज्यामितीय आकारहरूमा रङ मात्र प्रयोग गरिन्छ । बिलंपौ प्रायः ३–४ हातदेखि ८–१० हात वा १२ हातसम्म लामो हुन्छ र यस पद्धतिमा कपडामा ऐतिहासिक घटनाव्रmम, पौराणिक कथा, अवदान तथा जातककथाहरूलाई चित्रकथाका रूपमा उतारिन्छ । धकिंचित्र भन्नाले चित्र सहितको कपडालाई आगमकाठाका ढाकामा राखिने चित्र भन्ने बुझिन्छ । धकिंचित्रमा साङ्केतिक चिह्न वा देवीदेवताका चित्र हुन्छ । हलिपट चित्र भन्नालेलिङ्गोमा झुन्ड्याइने चित्र सहितको कपडा भन्ने बुझिन्छ । गाछिका चित्र भन्नाले देवीदेवताका रथमा राखेर जात्रागर्ने बेला रथको पछाडितर्पm राखिने चित्र सहितको कपडालाई भनिन्छ । इलांचित्र भन्नाले रथमा राखेर देवीदेवताकोजात्रा गर्ने बेला रथभित्र देवताको माथि राखिने चित्र सहितको कपडा भन्ने बुझिन्छ । गाछिका चित्र र इलां चित्र दुवैमा जुन देवताको जात्रा गरिने हो, सो देवतालाई साङ्केतिक आकार वा मानवीय स्वरूपमा चित्रण गरिन्छ ।
american_english: A painting executed on cloth is called 'Patachitra' in Sanskrit and Nepali, 'Paubha' in Nepal Bhasa, and 'Thangka' in Tibetan. Based on the size and format of the cloth and the characteristics of the painting style, Patachitra can be divided into seven types — Paubha painting, Patamandala, Bilampau, Dhakinchitra, Halipatachitra, Gachika painting, and Ilan painting. By Paubha painting is meant depictions on rectangular cloth of gods and goddesses, religious rituals, commemorations of specific historical events that occurred in society, social conditions, and natural and human-made scenes. In Patamandala, with the principal deity placed at the center on the cloth, small deities are painted within geometric shapes, or only colors are used within geometric shapes. Bilampau is usually 3–4 cubits to 8–10 cubits or up to 12 cubits long, and in this tradition, historical chronological sequences, mythological stories, Avadana, and Jataka tales are rendered on cloth in the form of pictorial narratives. By Dhakinchitra is understood an illustrated cloth that is placed over the screen of an Agam room. Dhakinchitra features symbolic signs or depictions of gods and goddesses. By Halipatachitra is understood an illustrated cloth that is hung from a ceremonial pole. Gachika painting refers to an illustrated cloth placed at the back of the chariot during a festival procession carrying gods and goddesses. By Ilan painting is understood an illustrated cloth placed above the deity inside the chariot during a festival procession carrying gods and goddesses. In both Gachika painting and Ilan painting, whichever deity is being paraded in the procession is depicted in symbolic form or in human form.

In both Gachika painting and Ilan painting, whichever deity is being paraded in the procession is depicted in symbolic form or in human form.

translator_notes: Preserved traditional Newar and Tibetan art terminology (Patachitra, Paubha, Thangka, Patamandala, Bilampau, Dhakinchitra, Halipatachitra, Gachika painting, Ilan painting, Agam room). Traditional measurement 'हात' (haat) translated as 'cubits'. Strict sentence-by-sentence order preserved across all variants.
